one_liner: Cloud email delivery platform for transactional and marketing email at scale

evidence.claim: Authentication is via API keys created in the SendGrid console
evidence.quote: Authenticate to the Twilio SendGrid API by creating an API Key in the Settings section of the Twilio SendGrid console

evidence.claim: The API key is sent as a Bearer token on every request; no OAuth flow exists
evidence.quote: SendGrid authenticates API requests with a static API key, sent on every request as the `Authorization: Bearer <key>` header.

evidence.claim: The API is RESTful, with SMTP relay also available
evidence.quote: The SendGrid Email API enables businesses to create, send, and manage emails at scale through RESTful APIs or SMTP relay.

evidence.claim: Self-serve account signup is publicly available
evidence.quote: Don't have a Twilio SendGrid account? Sign up now!

evidence.claim: No official SendGrid MCP server exists; only community servers
evidence.quote: There's no official SendGrid MCP server, and Twilio's alpha MCP covers none of SendGrid's APIs.

notes: API keys support Full Access or Custom Access scoping and are shown only once at creation. SMTP relay uses username 'apikey' with the API key as password (basic-style auth). Sending requires a verified Sender Identity or the API returns 403. Official docs cover a large v3 surface (mail send, marketing contacts, subusers, inbound parse, templates, stats). Twilio's own blog only shows how to build a community MCP server; multiple third-party MCP servers (Garoth/sendgrid-mcp, Pipedream) exist but are not vendor-official.
